appearances: Weathered cloak pinned with a tarnished brooch.
Sunburned skin and rope-calloused hands.
A long braid threaded with small bone beads.
One torn sleeve patched with mismatched cloth.
A deep scar crossing the left eyebrow.
Boots worn through at the heels, freshly re-stitched.
Silver hair cropped short despite a young face.
A jangling belt of keys, hooks, and small tools.
Ink stains from wrist to knuckles.
A chipped front tooth and an easy, crooked grin.
Freckles across the nose and a smudge of flour on the cheek.
A heavy traveler's pack that looks older than its owner.
One notched ear, the mark of an old dockside quarrel.
A fine coat gone shabby at the cuffs.
Burn marks on the fingertips of the favored hand.
A pendant of twisted iron worn against the skin.
Eyes the pale gray of winter river ice.
A limp that never quite slows the stride.
Rings on every finger, none of them matching.
A wide-brimmed hat with a feather from no bird anyone knows.
Gloves worn through at the fingertips, from writing or picking locks.
mannerisms: Counts every coin twice before it changes hands.
Taps a knuckle against the table when thinking.
Never sits with a door at their back.
Whistles an old marching tune while working.
Repeats your name three times when you meet.
Keeps one hand resting on a knife that never leaves the sheath.
Laughs a beat too late, then covers it with a cough.
Sniffs the air before entering any room.
Squints as if reading fine print in everything you say.
Circles every conversation back to a single topic.
Feeds crumbs to the birds between sentences.
Straightens crooked things — cups, frames, collars — without noticing.
Keeps a tally scratched into the tabletop.
Answers questions with questions first.
Hums when lying, though nobody has called it out yet.
Sets down any drink after exactly two sips.
Traces old scars with a thumb while talking.
Greets strangers like old friends and friends like strangers.
Never finishes a sentence when the wind changes.
Keeps a small ledger of favors owed and owed back.
Always stands where they can see both the entrance and the money.
personalities: Watchful and practical, slow to trust but loyal for life.
Warm on the surface, with a ledger of grudges underneath.
Endlessly curious about what things cost and why.
Tired of fighting, too stubborn to leave.
Cheerful in the way of people who have buried a lot.
Proud of a craft no one in town seems to need anymore.
Kind to children and animals, cold to everyone else.
Driven by a debt that is not written down anywhere.
Superstitious about rivers, doors, and the number nine.
Convinced the world is a story and hates the role it was given.
Gentle until someone threatens the plan.
Ambitious in the quiet, patient way that outlasts loud rivals.
Suspicious of magic, priests, and anyone offering help.
Bound by an oath spoken to someone now dead.
Optimistic enough to bet the rent on a good outcome.
More frightened of boredom than of bandits.
Honest, but reserves the right to choose the moment.
Keeps peace in the room the way others keep a blade.
Haunted by a success that should have been a failure.
Loves a rumor more than the truth, but knows the difference.
Patient with everyone except people who waste food.
motivations: Wants to buy back the family farm before winter.
Is saving every copper to move somewhere no one knows their name.
Seeks the person who carried their brother away from the battlefield.
Needs to prove the shipment was stolen, not sold.
Hopes the party will vouch for them with the town council.
Is searching for a scholar who can read an old letter.
Wants to see the sea once before settling down.
Is working off a fine imposed for a crime they didn't commit.
Seeks a cure for a sickness the local herbs can't touch.
Wants to reclaim a family heirloom held as evidence.
Is collecting testimony against a corrupt magistrate.
Hopes to earn a place in the guild before their sponsor retires.
Needs coin for a daughter's apprenticeship fee.
Is hunting the wolf pack that took the flock — and the shepherd.
Wants to restore a shrine the town has forgotten.
Is looking for someone brave enough to deliver a message.
Seeks an apprenticeship with a master who died last spring.
Wants to learn the name behind a stranger's kindness.
Is determined to reach the mountain pass before the first snow.
Hopes to trade a secret for a fresh start in another town.
Wants to hear their father's songs sung the way he sang them.
secrets: Owes a favor to a smuggler with a long memory.
Can read a language the town has never heard of.
Was the only witness to the mill fire — and lit the lamp.
Keeps a noble's illegitimate child hidden as an apprentice.
Sold the map that started the current feud.
Is quietly paying off the debts of an enemy.
Has been forging the guild's signatures for years.
Is a deserter from an army that still hangs deserters.
Buried something under the old shrine and never told a soul.
Takes orders from someone the party will meet later.
Cannot cast a single spell despite the priest's robes.
Knows which well the poison came from.
Is the reason the bridge tolls doubled.
Has a bounty on their head in the next duchy.
Carries letters between two houses that are not speaking.
Poisoned no one, but let the town believe it for protection.
Was paid to lose the last election for harbormaster.
Hears the river speak during floods and writes it down.
Is not the person whose name the party was given.
Keeps the only key to the crypt, and it is not in the church's inventory.
Sold their own name to a witch and answers to a borrowed one.
hooks: Asks the party to investigate a patrol that never returned.
Offers free lodging for a night in exchange for a discreet delivery.
Warns the party that the road east is watched by someone in uniform.
Begs the party to recover a lockbox from a sunken ferry.
Wants an escort to a shrine that bandits keep inspecting.
Invites the party to a dinner where everyone has an agenda.
Trades rumors for coin, and already has one about the party.
Needs someone to win a wrestling match without hurting the champion.
Asks the party to carry a sealed letter — unopened, no questions.
Offers to reveal a shortcut if the party finds their missing mule.
Wants a witness at a debt collection that might turn ugly.
Asks the party to judge a dispute between two fishing families.
Promises the location of a smuggler's cache for a vial of rare ink.
Needs the party to stall a wedding for exactly one hour.
Asks the party to escort a coffin nobody is allowed to open.
Wants the party to find out who has been feeding the wolves in the ravine.
Offers a map to a hot spring that is not on any chart.
Needs someone to retrieve a family sword from a pawnbroker gone quiet.
Asks the party to pose as merchants to test a new toll collector.
Wants the party in the market square at dawn, saying nothing.
Offers a fortune for one night's protection from the man with the ledger.

feature_intro.name: About
feature_intro.label: NPC generator
feature_intro.title: A table-ready NPC in one click
feature_intro.description: This free NPC generator builds an instant character for your session: a name, a role, an appearance, a mannerism, a personality, a motivation, a secret, and a plot hook — plus an optional D&D 5e-compatible stat block. No sign-up.

items.title: Everything a scene needs
items.description: Name, role, appearance, personality, motivation, secret, and hook are generated together, so the NPC is playable the moment it appears.

items.title: Narrative card or 5e stat block
items.description: Use Fantasy RPG mode for pure roleplay details, or D&D 5e mode to add armor class, hit points, and actions tuned to four power levels.

items.title: Free and instant
items.description: Generate NPCs right in your browser with no account — plan a whole town in an afternoon.

how_to_use.name: How to use
how_to_use.label: Four steps
how_to_use.title: From blank page to NPC at the table
how_to_use.description: The NPC generator is built for mid-prep panics and improvised towns alike.

items.title: Choose a mode
items.description: Pick Fantasy RPG for narrative-only NPCs or switch the NPC generator to D&D 5e for an optional stat block.

items.title: Generate
items.description: Set race, presentation, role, tone, and power level — or leave them on Random and let the dice decide.

items.title: Lock and reroll
items.description: Keep the parts you love by locking a field, then reroll the rest until the character clicks.

items.title: Copy or expand
items.description: Copy the card as Markdown or plain text for your notes, or send it to the backstory generator for a fuller history.

feature_benefits.name: Features
feature_benefits.label: Built for the table
feature_benefits.title: Small tools that make an NPC usable in seconds
feature_benefits.description: Every part of this random NPC generator aims at getting a character into play with minimal friction.

items.title: Narrative card plus stat block
items.description: The card covers roleplay; the optional 5e-compatible stat block covers combat so you never guess numbers mid-fight.

items.title: Per-field locks
items.description: Lock the name and motivation you like and reroll only the rest — controlled randomness instead of another full sheet.

items.title: Four power levels
items.description: Commoner to Elite templates scale the stat block from peasant witness to miniboss.

items.title: Two export formats
items.description: Markdown keeps formatting for your campaign wiki; plain text drops cleanly into any notes app or virtual tabletop.

feature_section.name: Use cases
feature_section.label: Made for
feature_section.title: Where a quick NPC saves the session
feature_section.description: From scheduled prep to the moment three players walk into an unnamed tavern, an NPC generator keeps the story moving.

items.title: Session prep
items.description: Flesh out the named cast before game night without building each one from scratch.

items.title: Improvised towns
items.description: When players befriend someone you never named, the random NPC generator produces shopkeeps, guards, and gossips on the spot.

items.title: One-shot nights
items.description: Spin up a whole supporting cast for a standalone evening in minutes.

items.title: PC side characters
items.description: Create family, rivals, and patrons for player characters, with enough detail to recur across arcs.

items.title: Is this NPC generator free?
items.description: Yes. Every name, word bank, stat block template, and export option is free, and there is no sign-up.

items.title: What is the difference between Fantasy RPG and D&D 5e mode?
items.description: Fantasy RPG mode generates roleplay details only — it does not use D&D 5e rules and produces no numbers. D&D 5e mode adds a stat block with armor class, hit points, abilities, and actions.

items.title: Is the stat block official?
items.description: No. It is a quick 5e-compatible reference built from original templates so a fight runs without page-flipping. It is not official balance, so adjust it freely for your table.

items.title: How do locks and rerolls work?
items.description: Generate a card, lock the fields you want to keep — the name, the secret, anything — and reroll the rest. Locked fields never change until you unlock them.

items.title: Do you save my NPCs?
items.description: No. Generation happens on the fly and nothing you create is stored on a server. What you keep lives in your notes and your clipboard.

items.title: How does the backstory handoff work?
items.description: Send a finished NPC to the DnD Backstory Generator and its details become the starting point for a longer character history you can edit.

cta_section.name: CTA
cta_section.title: Give your NPC a full history
cta_section.description: Happy with what the NPC generator gave you? Send the card to the DnD Backstory Generator to expand this character into a complete backstory with bonds, flaws, and a defining event.

related_tools.title: More free tools
related_tools.description: Companion generators for names, stories, and the rest of your table.
